candidate_relations.reason: The Holter recording confirms complete AV block as a component of the event, but the benchmark requires the full diagnostic object: vagus-mediated paroxysmal AV block (VP-AVB). The clinical context—syncope with gradual sinus slowing, progressive PR/PP prolongation, transient junctional escape, normal EP studies, no structural heart disease, and a vasovagal trigger setting (pre-operative)—all point specifically to autonomic/vagal etiology. 'Complete atrioventricular block' alone is a parent/component term that does not capture the paroxysmal, vagally-mediated mechanism required by the reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the conduction block type but omits the vagal/autonomic etiology and paroxysmal nature that define the benchmark diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Holter findings (gradual sinus slowing + PR prolongation before block onset) are classic for vagal rather than intrinsic conduction disease, supporting VP-AVB over idiopathic paroxysmal AV block
Normal EP studies explicitly exclude intrinsic conduction system disease, reinforcing autonomic etiology
